subject: Re: Order Form redlines — defining indemnity trigger & evidence package
messages:
From: Eliot Rodgers <eliot@nimcare.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: Anita Shah <anita.shah@nimcare.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form redlines — indemnity trigger definition and evidence package

Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal attached an Order Form with two main outstanding items related to indemnity: (1) the trigger for 'third-party IP claim' — they want a lower threshold language that would capture allegations based on model outputs even without an assertion of infringement, and (2) the evidence/notice requirements — they want a narrow set of deliverables from Redwood (detailed logs, prompt history, model version) but are pushing back on timelines.

High level asks from our side: can Redwood accept a trigger that requires a written notice from a third party or a court order (not mere allegation), and can you commit to preserving (for 90 days) the request-level KV/trace and prompt metadata so we can investigate?

Attaching our marked Order Form. Can you confirm whether Redwood has any operational constraints (retention, on-prem logs, or PII redaction) that would prevent producing the listed artifacts?

Appreciate a fast turnaround — procurement wants the contract wrapped by end of month.

— Eliot
Legal Ops, NimbusCare
(415) 555-0123

Attachments: Nimbus_OF_NIM_v3_marked.docx (docx)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Eliot Rodgers <eliot@nimcare.com>
Cc: Anita Shah <anita.shah@nimcare.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — indemnity trigger definition and evidence package

Eliot —

Thanks for the clear summary and the marked OF. We can move quickly on this. Short answers up front:
1) Trigger: Redwood is comfortable with a trigger that requires either (a) a written notice from a third party claiming infringement, or (b) a court/regulatory order. We want to avoid an open-ended 'allegation' trigger because operationally that creates 24/7 triage obligations for broad speculation.
2) Evidence/retention: We can commit to preserving request-level metadata and KV cache snapshots for 90 days for the specific requests associated with a claim, provided those requests do not contain customer PII that contradicts our retention policies. For high-sensitivity data (PII/PHI) we need a scoped process — see below.

I'm looping in Kim (legal) and Marissa (your account lead) to confirm firm contract language and commercial tradeoffs.

Proposed next step: Kim will suggest redline language for the MSA/Order Form that (i) defines the trigger as "written notice or court order," (ii) sets a 90-day evidence preservation window tied to a documented claim notice, and (iii) sets enumerated artifacts Redwood will provide (request logs, model version, prompt fingerprint, redacted KV cache). If that aligns, I can circulate a clean OF and an evidence checklist.

Jonas Weber
Director, Commercial
Redwood Inference

> On Tue, Mar 16, 2027 at 09:12, Eliot Rodgers <eliot@nimcare.com> wrote:
> > Jonas —
> > Thanks again for the demo last week...

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Eliot Rodgers <eliot@nimcare.com>, Anita Shah <anita.shah@nimcare.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 13:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — indemnity trigger definition and evidence package

Jonas / Marissa —

Thanks for looping me in. Draft guidance below that we can drop into the MSA/Order Form. I'm keeping it pragmatic to avoid turning this into a long-term ops burden.

1) Trigger language (MSA §12.2): "Customer's obligation to notify Redwood of a Claim shall be triggered by: (a) receipt by Customer of a written claim from a third party asserting that Customer's use of the Services infringes such third party's intellectual property rights; or (b) a binding court order or government injunction expressly identifying the Services."

2) Evidence preservation and scope: "On receipt of Customer's notice, Redwood will preserve for a period of ninety (90) days the Service request metadata, model version identifier, and a redacted KV cache snapshot associated with the alleged requests, to the extent retention is permitted by applicable law and Customer's data-handling instructions. Redwood will not be required to produce raw customer prompts or PII without a lawful process."

3) Operational SLA for delivery: propose a 14-business-day window for Redwood to deliver the enumerated artifacts after receipt of a valid legal request; if additional analysis is needed (forensics or expert review) parties will agree scope and timeline in writing.

4) Commercial concession: because this preservation/delivery has non-trivial cost, suggest a reciprocal obligation that Customer cooperates (timely access to its own logs, confirmation of data minimization) and a carveout for claims arising from Customer-provided prompts that knowingly infringe.

I'll prepare a redline snippet for the OF and an "evidence checklist" spreadsheet. Questions: do we want to commit to producing hashed prompt fingerprints (yes/no) or limit to metadata only? Hashes are less sensitive and help triage; I recommend including them.

Kim Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: Eliot Rodgers <eliot@nimcare.com>, Anita Shah <anita.shah@nimcare.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — indemnity trigger definition and evidence package

Team —

From a commercial standpoint: NimbusCare is a strategic early-adopter in healthcare vertical. They're pushing tight notice language but procurement is sensitive to timelines. If we make the 14-business-day delivery SLA firm, they may ask for a credit or discount for on-demand forensic pulls. Suggest we keep 14 days as target with a one-time "forensic pull" fee (cap TBD) that we can waive for mid-market deals but require for enterprise.

Marissa Cole
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

P.S. Eliot — we can flex on the forensic fee if Nimbus ups to a 12-month committed capacity. Will discuss in sync later this week.

From: Eliot Rodgers <eliot@nimcare.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: Anita Shah <anita.shah@nimcare.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 11:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — indemnity trigger definition and evidence package

Jonas / Kim / Marissa —

Appreciate the proposed language. A few clarifications from our counsel: (1) 14 business days for initial artifacts is acceptable if it includes hashed prompt fingerprints — that should materially help triage; (2) 90-day preservation sounds fair, but Nimbus needs an explicit commitment that Redwood will not auto-delete preserved artifacts during that window even if retention policies would otherwise apply; (3) we want a statement that Redwood will escalate claims to an identified Redwood technical liaison within 48 hours of notice.

If you can reflect those three points in the redline, procurement and legal will be comfortable. We can discuss the forensic fee in parallel but would prefer it be framed as an optional charge for non-standard analysis.

— Eliot

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Eliot Rodgers <eliot@nimcare.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 15:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: Proposed Order Form snippet + evidence checklist for NimbusCare

Eliot —

Thanks for the clarifications. I've incorporated your points into the attached materials: (a) updated OF redline with the "written notice or court order" trigger, explicit non-deletion commitment for the 90-day preservation window, and a clause requiring Redwood to designate an internal technical liaison within 48 hours of Customer notice; (b) an evidence checklist that enumerates artifacts we will provide (hashed prompt fingerprints, request metadata, model version id, redacted KV snapshot) and the 14-business-day delivery SLA.

Per commercial note: I've added language that the forensic-analysis fee is discretionary and can be waived if Nimbus commits to a 12-month reserved capacity at agreed AR commitment levels.

Please review the attachments and tell me if you'd like a short call to finalize. If acceptable, I'll route the clean OF to DocuSign and push the HubSpot deal to Contract Review stage.

Jonas Weber
Director, Commercial
Redwood Inference
